title: Halden Roasters
tagline: A coffee brand built like a field journal.
challenge: Halden had outgrown its farmers-market look. Twelve origins, three retail partners and a subscription launch needed one system that could flex without losing its voice.
approach: We built the identity around the roaster's own logbook: a stamped wordmark, a typographic origin grid and a colour code per roast level that works from bag to app.

process.title: Audit
process.text: Two days on the roastery floor, 40 competitor bags, one honest workshop.

process.title: Direction
process.text: Three territories. The logbook won on day one.

process.title: System
process.text: Wordmark, origin grid, roast colours, 14 bag variants.

process.title: Rollout
process.text: Packaging, café signage, subscription app and launch film.

outcome: The new range launched in 60 stores and the subscription sold out its first batch in four days.

title: Orbit Banking
challenge: Orbit's app did everything and explained nothing. New users dropped off before their first transfer.
approach: We rebuilt the core flows around one screen: where your money is, where it's going and what happens next, with motion that shows cause and effect.

process.title: Research
process.text: 24 user interviews and a full funnel teardown.

process.title: Architecture
process.text: Nine tabs cut to four. One home screen.

process.title: Interface
process.text: A component library of 180 parts, built with Orbit's engineers.

process.title: Motion
process.text: Transitions that trace every transfer end to end.

outcome: Onboarding completion rose sharply in the first quarter after release, and support tickets about transfers halved.

title: Tidewater Festival
challenge: A coastal arts festival in its tenth year needed to feel new again and reach an audience under 30.
approach: A single line that rises with the tide chart runs through every poster, story and stage screen. Each day of the festival gets its own tide.

process.title: Idea
process.text: The tide table as the festival's timetable.

process.title: Toolkit
process.text: A generative line tool the in-house team could run.

process.title: Campaign
process.text: Posters, OOH, 120 social assets, stage visuals.

process.title: Live
process.text: Real-time tide data on the main stage screens.

outcome: The festival sold out a week early, with its youngest audience on record.

title: Mora Skincare
challenge: Mora's formulas were serious; its packaging looked like everyone else's. It needed shelf presence in pharmacies and at premium retail.
approach: Uncoated tactile board, a single ingredient set in large type per product and a colour system drawn from the ingredients themselves.

process.title: Shelf study
process.text: Photographed 300 SKUs across 12 retailers.

process.title: Structure
process.text: One carton form, refillable glass, no plastic windows.

process.title: Graphics
process.text: Ingredient-led typography and a 9-colour palette.

process.title: Production
process.text: Press checks and print specs for three manufacturers.

outcome: Mora entered two national pharmacy chains within six months of the relaunch.

title: Signal FM Idents
tagline: A radio station you can watch.
challenge: Signal FM moved onto video platforms and had no visual language beyond a logo.
approach: We turned the station's audio waveform into a living logotype that reacts to whatever is on air, then built a library of idents around it.

process.title: Sound
process.text: Mapped the station's audio to shape, weight and speed.

process.title: Logotype
process.text: A variable wordmark driven by live audio.

process.title: Idents
process.text: 24 idents, stings and show openers.

process.title: Toolkit
process.text: Templates the station's editors use daily.

outcome: The idents now run across every stream and show, and the station's video audience has grown each month since launch.

title: Atlas Biennale
tagline: An exhibition you can read from across the room.
challenge: Forty pavilions, four languages and a site the size of a small town. Visitors kept getting lost.
approach: An oversized grid of numbers and arrows that works as signage, catalogue and website at once. Every pavilion got a number and a colour.

process.title: Wayfinding
process.text: Walked the site with the curators and mapped every route.

process.title: System
process.text: Numbers, arrows and a four-language type hierarchy.

process.title: Print
process.text: A 400-page catalogue and 1,200 signs.

process.title: Digital
process.text: A companion site built on the same grid.

outcome: Visitor surveys ranked navigation as the biennale's most improved area year on year.

title: Northline Outdoor
tagline: Gear for people who read the forecast twice.
challenge: A trusted technical outdoor brand looked dated next to newer, louder competitors.
approach: We kept the heritage mark, redrew it for small sizes and built a photographic style around real weather, real people and no retouching.

process.title: Heritage
process.text: Dug through 40 years of catalogues.

process.title: Mark
process.text: Redrawn for embroidery, tags and app icons.

process.title: Photography
process.text: Directed three shoots in actual bad weather.

process.title: Guidelines
process.text: A 90-page system for global retail partners.

outcome: The refresh rolled out across 14 markets without losing a single long-standing retail partner.

title: Parallel Records
tagline: One label, a hundred covers, zero templates.
challenge: An independent label releasing weekly needed covers that felt related without looking templated.
approach: A set of rules instead of a template: fixed type position, a shared grid and one photographic constraint per season. Every cover is different; the shelf still reads as Parallel.

process.title: Rules
process.text: Seven rules every cover must follow.

process.title: Covers
process.text: The first 30 releases, designed in-house with the label.

process.title: Motion
process.text: Animated covers for streaming platforms.

process.title: Handover
process.text: A rulebook so any designer can join in.

outcome: The label has released over 100 covers under the system, with six external designers contributing.
